a1.mp3: It opens up under the ear in a way I have not felt before. There is something in the lower strings that takes a moment to arrive and then fills the whole room. I would say it asks more of you than the other one did. You have to work for it, and when it answers, it answers.
a2.mp3: It does exactly what I ask, immediately, and it carries. I played the same passage on both and this is the one I could hear coming back to me from the far wall. It is not the more interesting instrument to sit with. It is the one I would take on stage tomorrow.
b1.mp3: Everyone sends me that study. What does it prove?
b2.mp3: If nobody can hear it, in what sense is it remarkable?
b3.mp3: That I accept. The work is real. Hearing it is another question.
b4.mp3: And the price? You think the price is nonsense.
b5.mp3: History, yes. Four hundred years of somebody keeping it alive.
b6.mp3: Let me ask you something. Would you buy a new one?
b7.mp3: A new one? After what I told you about the work?
b8.mp3: Playing it, not keeping it. Almost nobody says that out loud.
p1a.mp3: Although it cost several million, it came last.
p1b.mp3: Despite its price, it came last.
p2a.mp3: Although nobody could hear the difference, the work is real.
p2b.mp3: Despite nobody hearing the difference, the work is real.
p3a.mp3: Although they were wearing goggles, some still guessed right.
p3b.mp3: In spite of the goggles, some still guessed right.
p4a.mp3: Although the study is small, it has held up.
p4b.mp3: Despite the fact that the study is small, it has held up.
p5a.mp3: Although it is old, it is not better.
p5b.mp3: Despite being old, it is not better.
